name: Colombian Fried Plantains with Garlic Sauce (Patacones con Salsa de Ajo)

instructions.primary_message: FOR THE GARLIC SAUCE: Peel and mince garlic. Place in a small bowl.
Wash, dry, and juice lime into the bowl with the garlic.

Wash, dry, and shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add to the bowl, along with mayo, salt, and pepper, then whisk to combine the salsa de ajo. Place in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
instructions.secondary_message:
¼ small bunch cilantro
½ cup mayonnaise
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: FOR THE FRIED PLANTAINS: Trim both ends of the plantains, then score lengthwise at the natural ridges. Using your fingers, push into the score marks to lift and remove the peel. Cut plantains crosswise into 1-inch thick slices and place on a plate.

Place oil in a large skillet and heat over medium-high heat until the oil reaches 350ºF (the skillet should have about ½-inch of oil). Working in batches, add plantain slices to the skillet, flat-side down, and fry, flipping halfway through, until golden, about 2 minutes per side. Remove to a paper towel-lined plate. (Reserve skillet with oil for later use.)

Meanwhile, line a cutting board with wax paper. Working one at a time, place a fried plantain on the wax paper and cover with another second, smaller piece of wax paper. Using a flat-bottomed measuring cup or water glass, press down on the fried plantain slices to make ¼-inch thick rounds. Remove top layer of wax paper and return the plantain to the plate. Repeat until all plantains are pressed into rounds.

Return skillet (with oil) to medium-high heat. Once the oil is hot, working in batches, add plantains to the skillet and fry, flipping halfway through, until patacones are golden brown, 2 minutes per side. Remove to a fresh paper towel-lined plate and immediately season with salt.
TO SERVE: Arrange patacones on a plate or platter. Enjoy with salsa de ajo on the side for dipping!
